tagline: West along Whitefish Bay, with the freighters for company.
intro: From Brimley, on Waiska Bay, Lake Shore Drive heads west along Whitefish Bay through the Bay Mills Indian Community and into the Hiawatha National Forest. It is two paved lanes through northern hardwoods, conifers and wetlands, with waysides down to the Lake Superior shore, and it ends at M-123 south of Paradise.

The bay is a working one. Freighters bound to and from the Soo Locks use it, and the Canadian border runs through it. From the overlook at Mission Hill and Spectacle Lake you can watch them go by, with the white tower of Point Iroquois in view.

moments.title: Bay Mills Indian Community
moments.text: Its Ojibwe name is Gnoozhekaaning, the Place of the Pike, and its people have lived around Whitefish Bay for hundreds of years.

moments.title: Point Iroquois Light
moments.text: Built in 1870 where Whitefish Bay meets the St. Marys River, the white brick tower guided ships to and from the Soo Locks for 93 years, and it can still be climbed.

moments.title: Naomikong Point
moments.text: Now a low meadow, the point was pine forest when people came here, likely by the season, to fish, sometime between 100 and 900 CE, and left more than 100,000 potsherds behind.
